scenes.why: The hook is the problem itself, in the listing's own words: the first thing the right viewer recognises.
The turn: the product arrives after the problem, not before it.

caption.text: A record of what you actually did, kept as it happened, that you could hand to somebody at year's end.

scenes.why: Proof: the real screen that does what the problem asked for, captioned with the listing's own answer. Screen: "What we are doing today." (Today, per child: each lesson in the plan, and what is worth going over again.) chosen because it is the real screen closest to "A record of what you actually did, kept as it happened, that you could hand to s"; focus on "Ava".
Instagram Reel rewards a direct close: the real price against the real list price.

reasoning.decision: Instagram Reel, 1080×1920, 12–26s, hook by 1.2s, sound on
reasoning.because: Full-screen and swipeable: the first second decides whether anyone stays. Mostly watched with sound, but captions still carry every point. The right edge holds like/comment buttons and the bottom holds the caption, so text lives in the middle band.

reasoning.decision: Homeschooling Companion: $34 (list $69), motif "register", calm personality, cool accent #6a4a72
reasoning.because: From its definition and Shop listing. 3 real screens to show.

reasoning.decision: You already have a curriculum you chose on purpose and you want something that follows it rather than replacing it. / You teach more than one child and keeping their records separate in your head has stopped working.
reasoning.because: The listing's own audience lines; the director writes for them.

reasoning.decision: Problem cascade: Open on one real problem, let the related worries pile up, then cut to the product holding it.
reasoning.because: Best fit for a conversion film on Instagram Reel (platform fit 3, goal fit 2, already used on Instagram Reel ×1). Other candidates: What it is not (3.4), What you get (3.3).

reasoning.because: Problem 1 of the listing, "By March you can't remember what you covered in October.", answered by its own solution.

reasoning.decision: Transitions follow the product's own identity motif, "register"
reasoning.because: Transitions follow the product's own identity motif, "register": a register is filled line by line, so scenes are written in from the top.
Camera "float": a gentle float that keeps a held frame alive without demanding attention.
Grounds ink → light → light → accent: a cool accent, so a darker ground is used for contrast at a turn.
Sound-on placement: every transition, landing and reveal has a cue, and the bed ducks under the brand moment.
Each scene is held for the time its words take to read on Instagram Reel (0.26s a word), inside 12–26s.
